column1: # electron-runtime-deps.tsv — every shared library the OfficeWallNaglight shell
# artifact's Electron binary loads, and where the wall image gets it from.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A missing shared library is a BLACK WALL: Electron exits
# before it paints, `wall-kiosk.sh` restarts it every 3 s, and `[ -x ]` is still
# true so the "NOT INSTALLED" screen never fires either. The only diagnosis is
# after someone has walked over to it. Measured 2026-08-02 on a correct install
# with none of these packages present: Electron stops at
# "libnspr4.so: cannot open shared object file". The list is load-bearing, not
# HOW IT IS ENFORCED. vmtest/lib/common.sh's assert_electron_runtime_deps reads
# the DT_NEEDED list out of the binary that is about to be baked, and refuses to
# build if any soname is missing from this table, or if any `image-packages` row
# names a package the wall user-data does not install. So an Electron bump that
# adds a dependency fails the BUILD, with the soname named — it cannot reach the
#   1  soname          exactly as DT_NEEDED spells it
#   2  package         the Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) package that provides it
#   3  where           image-packages = must be in wall/user-data's packages:
#                      base           = in the base system, never listed
#                      bundled        = ships inside the artifact itself
# Package names verified against the noble archive 2026-08-02 (`apt-cache
# policy`); the soname -> package mapping was resolved with `dpkg -S`, not
# guessed. Note the `t64` suffixes: 24.04's 64-bit-time_t transition renamed
# libasound2, libatk*, libatspi, libcups and libglib, and the OLD names do not
# exist — an install would die at apt with "unable to locate package".
